2_Introduction: PSC with device efficiency (PCE) of 19.0678%, VOC of 1.0755 V, JSC of 24.654 mA/cm², and FF of 71.9142% was obtained. For the Cs0.05MA0.16FA0.79PbI2.9Br0.1, 1.73 mol/L perovskite precursor solution was prepared. For the fabrication of perovskite films, the perovskite solutions were spin-coated onto the substrates at 1000 rpm for 10 s and 5000 rpm for 30 s. A gentle antisolvent drop of 270 µL at last 8 s guided the perovskite crystals into a more ideal arrangement. Thermal annealing at 105 °C for 30 min improved crystal ordering and reduced defect density.
3_Result_Discussion: The Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₁₆FA₀.₇₉PbI₂.₉Br₀.₁ perovskite layer—engineered with a carefully balanced A-site cation mixture—exhibits enhanced phase stability and suppressed halide segregation due to the synergistic steric and electronic contributions of formamidinium (FA⁺) as the dominant cation, methylammonium (MA⁺) for lattice strain relaxation, and cesium (Cs⁺) for tolerance factor optimization (t ≈ 0.92), while the Br⁻ incorporation at the X-site fine-tunes the bandgap (~1.58 eV) and mitigates iodide vacancy formation; its crystallization kinetics are precisely governed by the 1.73 mol/L precursor concentration, which avoids excessive nucleation density or premature aggregation, the dual-speed spin-coating protocol (1000 rpm/10 s for uniform wet-film formation followed by 5000 rpm/30 s for rapid solvent extraction), and critically, the antisolvent quenching at the 8 s mark—where the 270 µL chlorobenzene drop induces instantaneous supersaturation just as the intermediate solvate phase begins to desolvate, thereby promoting oriented nucleation and suppressing random grain boundary formation; subsequent thermal annealing at 105 °C for 30 min drives complete ligand expulsion, facilitates Pb–I framework reorganization, relieves residual tensile stress evidenced by narrowed XRD (001) peak FWHM and absence of parasitic PbI₂ reflections at ~12.6°, and enables defect healing through halide redistribution—collectively yielding high crystallinity, low trap-state density, and improved carrier diffusion length. Morphological characterization reveals near-complete film coverage (>99.2% continuity) with uniform grayscale intensity across PL mapping, indicating homogeneous nucleation and absence of pinholes or dewetted domains, while time-resolved PL shows a monoexponential decay with τₐᵥₑ = 1.24 µs and >3.5× enhancement in integrated PL intensity versus control, directly corroborating suppressed non-radiative recombination at grain boundaries and surfaces; these structural, morphological, and optical signatures jointly confirm that the optimized crystallization protocol achieves both thermodynamic phase purity and kinetic control over defect evolution, enabling efficient charge extraction and minimal voltage losses at the buried interface. VOC of 1.0755 V, JSC of 24.654 mA/cm², FF of 71.9142%, and PCE of 19.0678% were achieved.
